findings.reason: the arm names a comparison the cited artefacts cannot support, so the node would either stall on it or fabricate the agreement; the clause needs the times it actually has (the imasdb read's own slices, and the validator reference at its own four times, stated as a separate check), or the arm dropped.
findings.text: §2 done-when (1) requires the translated DD3 read to agree in sign with the DD 4.1.0 validator layers "at their shared times", but the two artefacts share no times: the imasdb pulse `/work/imas/shared/imasdb/ITER/3/130506/6` carries 56 equilibrium slices from 2.0 s to 102.5 s (Ip up to 15.0 MA; 55 of 56 above 1 MA, matching the census row), while the validator case's four slices are the ones `tests/test_forward_profile_corsica.py:57,168` asserts, `SLICE_TIMES = (150.0, 200.0, 230.0, 231.0)` — read from the registry case `iter_corsica_130506`, which the plan itself now describes as a validator input/reference pair rather than a conversion of the pulse. The clause is therefore not measurable on the record the repository holds: a node obeying it either fails on an empty join or, worse, pairs slices by index and reports a sign agreement between different physical times as if it were the DD3→DD4 cross-check

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `ITER/3/130506/6` exists and opens at DD 3.41.0; the manifest entry `iter_corsica_130506` exists with `input`/`reference` layers, both DD 4.1.0; `nova/io/cocos.py` exists and has no importer outside its own docstring; `cocos_from_digits`, `determine_digits` and `flux_loop_two_pi_ratio` resolve in `nova/scripts/identify_source_cocos.py`; `SourceSignal.convention_factor`, `BlockedSignal` and `nova_cocos` imports resolve in `nova/io/sourcemap.py`; `PROFILE_RESIDUAL_RMS`, `ScorecardField`, `_profile_reproduction_residuals`, `TOTAL_FLUX_FACTOR`, `grad_shafranov_source` and `CerfonFreidbergSingleNull` all resolve. No extensionless href in the plan.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2 done-when (1)'s cross-check arm ("agrees in sign with the repository's DD 4.1.0 validator layers of the same case at their shared times") names a time set the two cited artefacts do not share, so the arm cannot be executed as written; the other clauses (`refused by name`, the planted-copy positive control, `negate ψ … and the read is refused`) are measurable and the negative control is declared.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §2's evidence is the census/measure record under `docs/research/` (in git, served by the reckon surface: `/nova/research/dd-cocos-census`), not a scratchpad or node-local path; §5 writes into the same record.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §2's symbols are mechanism-named (`determine_digits`, `cocos_from_digits`, `convention_factor`, `BlockedSignal`); no plan label, ticket or version tag, and no changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the root cause §0 states matches its evidence (the measured `PlasmaSource.prescribe` guard refusing the conforming COCOS 11 ITER sources), and §2's mechanism runs on real callers (`nova/scripts/identify_source_cocos.py:1692` for the verdict line, `PlasmaSource.from_imas` for the reader path, `nova/io/sourcemap.py`'s existing `convention_transform` factors); the one arm whose premise its cited evidence does not support is reported under `done_when` below.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 delivers one entry point (a DD3→17 translator with DD4 passthrough and the conformance refusal), spoken of as one module at a reader boundary.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every `data-links` on §2–§5 matches the `plan-section-depends-on` map (`s2→s1`, `s3→s2`, `s4→s3`, `s5→s1,s2`), and each target section exists.
